source_quality.source_metadata_note: Native 1280x720 originals accepted after source and visual review. Final graphics are 1080p; the footage is not claimed as native 1080p.

native_hd_review.reason: S02E03, S02E06 and S02E08 are native 1280x720 English originals at the highest quality offered to this account. Native frames of the opening, confrontations, gift and later coat discovery were examined. Full audio/video decodes passed. No burned subtitles or added watermark observed; the originals were not upscaled.

outro_summary: Richie returns expecting his old reputation to buy authority. Tony turns the poker dispute into a financial penalty. The jacket becomes another attempt to recover status, then ends up on somebody else. Richie can argue about the rules. Tony still gets to enforce them.

opening.speaker: white
opening.label: Richie
opening.evidence: Native opening images and local English ASR confirm Richie speaks before Tony. The cut retains the full lead-in.

annotations.speaker: white
annotations.comment: Richie opens with a complaint about being avoided. He expects his return to restore the old relationship automatically. Before discussing business, he wants Tony to explain the welcome.
annotations.review_method: Actual episode timing reference and scene evidence reviewed; original editorial comment. No human audio listening claimed.

annotations.speaker: black
annotations.comment: Tony answers the behaviour instead of the grievance: his position makes open business discussions risky. A meeting in a mall is a precaution, rather than proof that Richie has been demoted.
annotations.review_method: Actual episode timing reference and scene evidence reviewed; original editorial comment. No human audio listening claimed.

annotations.speaker: white
annotations.comment: Richie reaches for an old favour. It gives him something concrete to claim instead of merely describing his feelings. The opening has changed from a complaint to an invoice.
annotations.review_method: Actual episode timing reference and scene evidence reviewed; original editorial comment. No human audio listening claimed.

annotations.speaker: black
annotations.comment: Tony challenges whether Richie ever helped him, leaving an obvious old incident available as a reply. He could explain the present rules without disputing a favour Richie can identify.
annotations.review_method: Actual episode timing reference and scene evidence reviewed; original editorial comment. No human audio listening claimed.

annotations.speaker: white
annotations.comment: Richie supplies the actual incident: the robbery of Feech's game and the protection he provided afterward. He answers the challenge directly, without having to prove that the favour still buys authority.
annotations.review_method: Actual episode timing reference and scene evidence reviewed; original editorial comment. No human audio listening claimed.

annotations.speaker: black
annotations.comment: Tony offers reassurance and restoration over time. It is a sensible way to lower the temperature, although it leaves Richie free to challenge whether Tony has the right to grant what used to be his.
annotations.review_method: Actual episode timing reference and scene evidence reviewed; original editorial comment. No human audio listening claimed.

annotations.speaker: white
annotations.comment: Richie treats his old position as a permanent property right. The distinction sounds forceful, but rejecting the offer leaves him no practical route to the business he wants restored.
annotations.review_method: Actual episode timing reference and scene evidence reviewed; original editorial comment. No human audio listening claimed.

annotations.speaker: white
annotations.comment: Calling the current boss kid keeps the argument inside the hierarchy Richie remembers. He wants recognition, yet signals that he does not recognise the authority of the person granting it.
annotations.review_method: Actual episode timing reference and scene evidence reviewed; original editorial comment. No human audio listening claimed.

annotations.speaker: black
annotations.comment: Tony turns the general demand to be careful into a specific example: Beansie and the attempted shake-down. The warning now has an identifiable action and an identifiable boundary.
annotations.review_method: Actual episode timing reference and scene evidence reviewed; original editorial comment. No human audio listening claimed.

annotations.speaker: white
annotations.comment: Richie reframes the conflict as loyalty to an outsider over one of their own. It is more relevant than an old entitlement, but it still does not answer Tony's instruction to leave Beansie alone.
annotations.review_method: Actual episode timing reference and scene evidence reviewed; original editorial comment. No human audio listening claimed.

annotations.speaker: black
annotations.comment: Tony presents the instruction as a favour and then says Richie can refuse. The hostile phrasing blurs the boundary he just established. It is not permission to attack Beansie, but it is avoidable ambiguity.
annotations.review_method: Actual episode timing reference and scene evidence reviewed; original editorial comment. No human audio listening claimed.

annotations.speaker: black
annotations.comment: Tony hears an insult in a question about his sister. Richie clarifies that he means Janice, and Tony admits the misunderstanding. The boss has briefly started an argument with his own interpretation.
annotations.review_method: Actual episode timing reference and scene evidence reviewed; original editorial comment. No human audio listening claimed.

annotations.speaker: white
annotations.comment: Richie answers the warning with a joke about putting the car in drive. After ignoring a direct instruction, he is making defiance explicit. A punchline is not a defence against the consequences.
annotations.review_method: Actual episode timing reference and scene evidence reviewed; original editorial comment. No human audio listening claimed.

annotations.speaker: black
annotations.comment: Tony challenges Richie's claim to the old standards by asking what he has done for anybody else. The reply meets the justification on its own terms, without accepting it as an excuse.
annotations.review_method: Actual episode timing reference and scene evidence reviewed; original editorial comment. No human audio listening claimed.

annotations.speaker: black
annotations.comment: Tony states the hierarchy without a favour or an opt-out this time. Respect for the office is a requirement. Richie no longer has room to reinterpret the order as a personal request.
annotations.review_method: Actual episode timing reference and scene evidence reviewed; original editorial comment. No human audio listening claimed.

annotations.speaker: white
annotations.comment: Richie finally acknowledges the instruction instead of arguing about the old days. The reply prevents further escalation, although saying all right does not recover the ground already lost.
annotations.review_method: Actual episode timing reference and scene evidence reviewed; original editorial comment. No human audio listening claimed.

annotations.speaker: white
annotations.comment: Richie threatens Davey inside Tony's game. Whatever the debt, he has chosen a setting where his method challenges the host's control. A collection problem is becoming an authority problem.
annotations.review_method: Actual episode timing reference and scene evidence reviewed; original editorial comment. No human audio listening claimed.

annotations.speaker: white
annotations.comment: Richie explains that Davey ignored the restriction he imposed. The grievance is real, but it explains the anger rather than justifying the disruption. He still needs to answer for the location.
annotations.review_method: Actual episode timing reference and scene evidence reviewed; original editorial comment. No human audio listening claimed.

annotations.speaker: black
annotations.comment: Tony separates the debt from the conduct: why does Davey owing money permit disrespecting this game? The direct question prevents Richie from using one valid complaint to excuse a different act.
annotations.review_method: Actual episode timing reference and scene evidence reviewed; original editorial comment. No human audio listening claimed.

annotations.speaker: white
annotations.comment: Richie invokes unnamed people who also dislike Tony's attitude. He turns a dispute about a debtor into a suggestion of opposition, without naming anybody willing to stand behind it.
annotations.review_method: Actual episode timing reference and scene evidence reviewed; original editorial comment. No human audio listening claimed.

annotations.speaker: white
annotations.comment: Richie returns to an amount owed and a specific request to see the debtor. This is better than unnamed dissent, but it does not undo the disruption. The permission is still missing.
annotations.review_method: Actual episode timing reference and scene evidence reviewed; original editorial comment. No human audio listening claimed.

annotations.speaker: black
annotations.comment: Tony controls access to the debtor instead of letting Richie dictate collection. Richie leaves; the player stays. The dispute ends with a decision Tony can enforce, rather than another exchange of insults.
annotations.review_method: Actual episode timing reference and scene evidence reviewed; original editorial comment. No human audio listening claimed.

annotations.speaker: white
annotations.comment: An actual apology is a sensible reset of the tone. Richie names the disruption instead of defending it. Unfortunately, saying sorry does not come with a refund for the position.
annotations.review_method: Actual episode timing reference and scene evidence reviewed; original editorial comment. No human audio listening claimed.

annotations.speaker: black
annotations.comment: Tony makes the requirement clear: respect the title and stop crossing its boundaries. Richie is not being asked to admire him. He is being asked to recognise the office.
annotations.review_method: Actual episode timing reference and scene evidence reviewed; original editorial comment. No human audio listening claimed.

annotations.speaker: white
annotations.comment: Richie concedes control while portraying the rules as Tony's personal whim. It sounds like agreement, but it keeps the original grievance alive. The apology has acquired a footnote.
annotations.review_method: Actual episode timing reference and scene evidence reviewed; original editorial comment. No human audio listening claimed.

annotations.speaker: black
annotations.comment: Tony rejects the claim that he has invented a private rulebook. The answer keeps the argument on an existing hierarchy, rather than accepting a debate about his personal preferences.
annotations.review_method: Actual episode timing reference and scene evidence reviewed; original editorial comment. No human audio listening claimed.

annotations.speaker: black
annotations.comment: Tony converts the dispute about respect into an enforceable cost: his debt gets paid first. Richie loses collection priority and the ability to dismiss the conversation as merely personal.
annotations.review_method: Actual episode timing reference and scene evidence reviewed; original editorial comment. No human audio listening claimed.

annotations.speaker: black
annotations.comment: Tony opens with a joke, but he asks the question and Richie must explain the visit. A friendly greeting, by New Jersey standards. The person choosing the subject keeps the initiative.
annotations.review_method: Actual episode timing reference and scene evidence reviewed; original editorial comment. No human audio listening claimed.

annotations.speaker: white
annotations.comment: Richie answers a current instruction with an old debt to Jackie. He is trying to pay today's bill with yesterday's reputation. It does not explain why the ramp should remain unbuilt.
annotations.review_method: Actual episode timing reference and scene evidence reviewed; original editorial comment. No human audio listening claimed.

annotations.speaker: black
annotations.comment: Tony refuses the historical detour. The instruction stays short, specific and unchanged. He does not need to win an argument about Jackie to insist that Richie build the ramp.
annotations.review_method: Actual episode timing reference and scene evidence reviewed; original editorial comment. No human audio listening claimed.

annotations.speaker: white
annotations.comment: With the obligation acknowledged, Richie changes the mood through a gift. A familiar peace offering is more useful than another refusal. The jacket arrives before its extensive user manual.
annotations.review_method: Actual episode timing reference and scene evidence reviewed; original editorial comment. No human audio listening claimed.

annotations.speaker: white
annotations.comment: Richie sells the jacket through the reputation of the man he beat. Junior supplies an unrelated ending, and the intimidating legend becomes awkward small talk. The pitch has gained a co-author.
annotations.review_method: Actual episode timing reference and scene evidence reviewed; original editorial comment. No human audio listening claimed.

annotations.speaker: black
annotations.comment: Tony compliments the object without accepting the rank attached to its story. A courteous answer is enough. The receipt says leather jacket; it does not say promotion.
annotations.review_method: Actual episode timing reference and scene evidence reviewed; original editorial comment. No human audio listening claimed.

annotations.speaker: white
annotations.comment: Richie says he is letting go of the past while asking Tony to wear its biggest souvenir. The gift may be sincere, but the sales pitch still lives in the hierarchy he remembers.
annotations.review_method: Actual episode timing reference and scene evidence reviewed; original editorial comment. No human audio listening claimed.

annotations.speaker: black
annotations.comment: Tony wears the coat and thanks him. That completes the exchange without promising to display it forever or treat Richie differently. Accepting a present is not accepting a contract.
annotations.review_method: Actual episode timing reference and scene evidence reviewed; original editorial comment. No human audio listening claimed.

annotations.speaker: white
annotations.comment: Richie checks the jacket's status in front of the family. Tony gives a polite answer, not a commitment. The question gets reassurance; it does not establish that the gift has changed their relationship.
annotations.review_method: Actual episode timing reference and scene evidence reviewed; original editorial comment. No human audio listening claimed.

annotations.speaker: white
annotations.comment: Richie turns the gift into a demand for visible proof. Why is Tony not wearing it? The present now comes with a dress code, and the recipient is being asked to justify his wardrobe.
annotations.review_method: Actual episode timing reference and scene evidence reviewed; original editorial comment. No human audio listening claimed.

annotations.speaker: black
annotations.comment: Tony answers the practical question and offers the jacket back. He refuses the implied obligation without starting another argument over its history. Richie can reclaim the object or stop policing it.
annotations.review_method: Actual episode timing reference and scene evidence reviewed; original editorial comment. No human audio listening claimed.

annotations.speaker: white
annotations.comment: Richie repeats the Rocco DiMeo story instead of answering the offer. The jacket's history is not missing information. Repeating it still cannot establish an obligation to wear it.
annotations.review_method: Actual episode timing reference and scene evidence reviewed; original editorial comment. No human audio listening claimed.

annotations.speaker: white
annotations.comment: The trophy meant to restore Richie's status is now on somebody else. He sees it, says he is fine, and leaves. The gift has failed as an authority badge; Tony's private intention is not established.
annotations.review_method: Actual episode timing reference and scene evidence reviewed; original editorial comment. No human audio listening claimed.
